day1.text: Hi, I'm Lira! The Sun sent a big cloud our way — it will fly for a few days.

day2.text: The Sun flared again and sent two more clouds toward us.

day3.text: A small flare on the Sun, and people on Earth can see the northern lights!

day4.text: The Sun is totally quiet today — a great day for base chores.

day5.text: The solar clouds have flown for 4 days — and they're almost here!

day6.text: A few flares on the Sun, but they won't reach us.

day7.text: The Sun sent three more clouds — they'll arrive in 3 days.

day8.text: One more cloud is flying behind and catching up with the others.

day9.text: The Sun is a bit calmer, and the clouds arrive tomorrow.

day10.text: The clouds are about to cover the Moon — good thing we knew in advance!

day11.text: The Sun is shining bright, and the batteries charge well.

day12.text: The quietest day of the week — no strong flares at all.

day13.text: The Sun is slowly setting: the long night is coming.

day14.text: The last sunny day before a two-week night!

day15.text: The lunar night has come: no sun, so save your energy.

day16.text: It's dark and cold, but Mission Control sends Sun news every day.

day17.text: A very strong flare! Radio contact with Earth may be lost tomorrow.

day18.text: No contact with Earth — the radio is noisy after yesterday's flare.

day19.text: Two strong flares in a row — the Sun is very restless!

day20.text: The clouds we knew about are coming, and there's no radio contact.

day21.text: A huge spot has grown on the Sun — 15 times wider than Earth!

day22.text: The giant spot flared again. A big storm is coming soon.

day23.text: A radiation storm is starting: the Sun sent very fast particles!

day24.text: The strongest storm in 20 years, and the particles keep coming!

day25.text: The strongest flare of the whole mission, and the storm goes on!

day26.text: Another flare, and the crew is tired of sitting in the shelter.

day27.text: A new radiation storm! Hang on, sunrise is close.

day28.text: The strongest flare since 2017 — but the spot is already turning away.

day29.text: Sunrise! We fly home tomorrow, but the Sun is flaring again.

day30.text: Departure day! The Sun is finally calm.
